messages:
maya: Quick q — the new "stamp allocator" on the Cost dashboard is showing negative unit cost for some low-volume routes. Anyone seen this?
devin: saw a couple of those yesterday in the smoke tests. looks like cache credits > billed tokens in the rollup for tiny sessions.
chris: negative unit cost = sign we're subtracting cache savings incorrectly at the per-route stage. probably double-counting a global cache credit.
sarah: do we have the exact calculation being used in the UI? I remember an earlier PR that moved some of aggregation to client-side.
kevin: client-side aggregations exist for sparkline previews, but the authoritative numbers come from the stamp-allocator service. it emits per-route "token_charge" and "cache_credit" metrics.
maya: can you paste the stamp-allocator output for an example route? I'm seeing: route /embed/search -> total_tokens=120, billed_tokens=10, cache_credit=40. UI shows unit_cost = -0.03.
devin: that combination implies we subtract cache_credit directly from billed_tokens, not from cost. if cache_credit is in token-equivalent units but billed_tokens already includes some cache-adjusted measure, we end up overcompensating.
alison: also we added a sticky-routing experiment last week that routes warm cache hits to the dedicated pool. those hits were getting both a route-level cache_credit and a global "KV-prefix" cache credit.
chris: bingo. double crediting. two possible fixes: 1) stamp-allocator emits a bool "credit_is_global" and UI subtracts only route-level credits; 2) change backend rollup to normalize credits to a single namespace before exporting.
sarah: preference for backend-normalize (2). UI logic is brittle and we've had other bugs caused by client math.
kevin: backend-normalize means changing the aggregator pipeline. should be low risk: insert a dedupe stage that groups on (tenant, route, cache_scope) and folds credits.
maya: what's the rollout plan? we need to avoid a flash change in reported costs for customers.
devin: propose: deploy normalized rollup as a new metric name: `token_cost_v2` and keep current v1. Wire the dashboard to show v2 behind a toggle. monitor diffs for 24h, then flip.
chris: +1. small DB migration: update views that compute per-tenant rollups. also add a sampling flag to emit both v1/v2 for 7 days.
alison: UX thing — the dashboard should annotate that numbers are in "experimental normalization" when users toggle v2. we should also show delta % on the route list so SREs can spot big jumps.
kevin: telemetry: emit a histogram of (v2 - v1) per-route, and a breakdown by model_sku and by session_length bucket. that will help detect regressions where v2 accidentally downgrades crediting for legitimate multi-tenant caches.
sarah: will the quota system be affected? if billed_tokens shrink or grow, quota usage could trigger unexpected rate limits.
devin: good catch — quota checks are evaluated on the raw request path before rollup. we only change reporting and billing pipelines, so runtime quotas unaffected. but customer-facing quota pages (console) will display different usage numbers after flip. need comms.
maya: action items:
- devin: prototype v2 aggregator and emit parallel metrics (ETA 2d)
- chris: add dedupe stage to aggregator pipeline + unit tests (ETA 3d)
- kevin: add telemetry histograms & sampling (ETA 2d)
- alison: design toggle + delta badges + copy for experimental label (ETA 4d)
- sarah: draft customer comms and internal runbook for the flip (ETA 2d)
- maya: coordinate canary and monitor thresholds (I'll own)
ops-bot: Deploy bot: "stamp-allocator-v2" deployed to canary cluster (canary-3) at 2231104780 :rocket:
chris: canary looks good on 10k reqs/min. diffs median ~0.2% but tail routes show -35% to +12%.
kevin: those -35% tails correlate with routes that have cross-tenant KV caches (we're now attributing global credits to the route less aggressively).
maya: ok let's keep canary running and gather histograms for 24h. do not flip dashboard yet.
devin: also adding a quick fix if customers query anomalies: endpoint `/admin/credit-debug?route=` returns raw contributions (global credits, route credits, sampling flag).
alison: thanks — once we have the toggle UX, can we surface a short FAQ: "Why did my route cost change?" with examples and how to opt into legacy view for 7 days.
sarah: noted for runbook. we should also add an alert if any route sees >50% negative delta (v2 - v1) on rolling 1h.
maya: perfect. thanks all. i'll ping #product-updates once we flip and compile a short snippet for the billing team. :thumbsup:
kevin: one more note — double-check the quantization step for token-cost-per-model. v2 assumes tokens -> cost mapping uses model_sku price table; v1 applied a per-request discount that we forgot to port. that could explain some +12% increases.
chris: good catch, adding to test matrix.
maya: cool. we'll reconvene after 24h of canary telemetry.
ops-bot: Alertbot: Rolling histogram collection complete for canary-3 — samples=1,024,876; median delta=0.18%; tail95 delta=-12.7%
devin: sharing table:```
route | v1_cost | v2_cost | delta%
/search | 12.34 | 12.18 | -1.3%
/embed/search | 0.61 | 0.40 | -34.4%
/chat/resume | 7.12 | 7.20 | +1.1%
```
alison: that /embed/search row is the one we started with. good to have evidence. I'll draft the UX copy now.
maya: thanks team — great work triaging. follow-ups in the TODOs above.
